topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Logic of Movement
target_audience: High school students or introductory computer science learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Binary
lecture_lines: Each position represents a power of two.
Combine powers to form any number.
animations: Show binary count mapping to decimal 0-7.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Challenge
lecture_lines: Three rods hold disks of varying sizes.
Move one disk at a time.
Never place larger on smaller disks.
animations: Display three pegs with disks stacked by size.
Show one disk move from peg A to C.
Show recursive move: n-1 disks move.

sections.title: Connecting Moves to Binary Counting
lecture_lines: Binary counting maps to disk moves.
Changing bits dictate which disk moves.
animations: Map disks on pegs to binary 0 and 1.
Highlight disk movement matching bit changes.
Show sequence: disk 1 moves, bit changes.
Show sequence: disk 2 moves, bit changes.
Finalize alignment: binary states reflect peg configurations.

sections.title: Application: The Cosmic Clock
animations: Move clock hand as binary counter ticks.
Show clock hand reaching final position.
